newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to softer.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to softer.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were steady to softer as underlying markets recouped most of their early losses and time-decay weighed on front-end premiums, dealers said.

"A good part of the activity was related to dealers and small funds just basically trading this range going into the weekend," said a Treasury bond trader for an investment bank trader at Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options was unchanged at around 9.8 percent, while December, which expires next Friday, lost 0.2 point at about 7.8 percent.

"The important thing that happened today was the market (December T-bond futures) traded down to 113-22/32 and held there," he added. He said that level represented one standard deviation below Thursday's close on a daily basis.
December futures closed an abbreviated session 7/32 down at 114-2/32. CBOT T-bond trading was shortened due to the Veterans Day holiday on Monday.
With January serial options going on board at the start of next week, traders said activity in December options was mostly position-squaring ahead of expiration.

But they added the short-dated December contracts could expect some bids by gamma players early next week ahead of U.S. inflation data and Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, although most traders did not expect any near-term changes in the Federal Reserve monetary policy.
October producer price index (PPI) is due for release on Wednesday and consumer price index (CPI) on Thursday.
Premiums on shorter maturity options, which have high gamma values, accelerate more quickly per change in the underlying than those on longer dated contracts.
In the Eurodollar pit at Chicago Mercantile Exchange, volatilities were mostly easier. Implied volatility for March futures options was off 0.3 point to 11.6 percent.
Apart from a few large deals, volume was light overall with little directionality bias, a brokerage trader at CME said.
An investment bank was said to have sold 4,000 contracts of March 94.50 calls, while a second bank was seen buying 3,000 lots of June 95.00 calls hedged against futures.
CME Eurodollar trading closes early on Monday.
